1. Overview
The data protection policy ensures to safeguard sensitive information owned by
Emaratech and its subsidiaries and ensure compliance with legal and regulatory
requirements. The policy establishes requirements for data security measures and to
mitigate the risks related to unauthorized disclosure of data.
This policy is aligned with the requirements of applicable information security
standards and regulations including UAE Information Assurance Regulation v1.1, DESC
Information Security Regulation v3.0, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and PCI DSS v4.0.
2. Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to establish requirements to ensure responsible handling,
processing, and protection of Emaratech, its subsidiaries, and their client’s sensitive
information they collect from customers, employees, and other stakeholders.
3. Scope
3.1. This policy applies to all information assets owned and managed by Emaratech
and its subsidiaries which include information, people, processes, and
technology assets that support business processes and services.
3.2. This policy applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party vendors
(hereafter referred to as ‘Users’) having access to Emaratech and its
subsidiaries’ information assets.

4. Roles and Responsibilities
4.1. Information Technology/Infrastructure Management Department (IT/IMD) is
responsible for:
a) Protect records according to their information security classification.
b) Ensure sensitive data is protected using appropriate masking techniques.
c) Implementing technical controls required to ensure data protection on
information assets.
d) Choose data storage systems that allow for the timely and proper retrieval of
records.
e) Reviewing the security controls periodically to ensure compliance with this
policy.
4.2. Information Security Department (ISD) is responsible for:
a) Ensuring that the policy is communicated to all the users.
b) Conducting periodic checks to ensure compliance with the policy.
4.3. Head of Departments (HoDs) are responsible for:
a) Ensuring the compliance with the Data Protection policy within their
respective departments.
b) Providing support to the subordinates to ensure compliance with the Data
Protection Policy.
4.4. Users are responsible for:
a) Adhering to the requirements mentioned in the Data Protection Policy.

c) Reporting any social media incidents, breaches or potential issues to the ISD.

6. Glossary
6.1. Terms and Definitions
Term Definition
Integrity The condition of a record being complete and unaltered.
Retention
Schedule
A timetable that specifies the period records must be kept
before they are destroyed or archived.
Data Masking A technique used to hide original data with modified content
(characters or other data) to protect sensitive information.
Pseudonymization A data management procedure by which personally
identifiable information fields within a data record are
replaced by one or more artificial identifiers, or pseudonyms.
Anonymization The process of removing personally identifiable information
from data sets, so that the people whom the data describe
remain anonymous.
Digital Signatures A digital code generated and authenticated by public key
encryption, attached to an electronically transmitted
document to verify its contents and the sender's identity.
Encryption The process of converting data into a code to prevent
unauthorized access.
Sensitive
Information
Information that must be protected from unauthorized access
to safeguard the privacy or security of an individual or
organization.
Obfuscation The act of making data unclear or unintelligible to
unauthorized users.

7. Policy Requirements
7.1. Protection of Records
7.1.1 Emaratech and its subsidiaries shall protect the authenticity, reliability, integrity
and usability of records.
7.1.2 IT/IMD shall store, handle chain of custody and dispose of records, prevent
manipulation of records in accordance with Data Retention and Disposal Policy
(Document Number: ISD-ISMS-SPOL-15) and Information Asset Management
Policy (Document Number: ISD-ISMS-SPOL-18).
7.1.3 ISD shall define a retention schedule defining records and the period for which
they shall be retained in line with applicable laws and regulations.
7.1.4 Where possible, the defined retention period shall be configured in the system
to permit appropriate destruction of records after that period.
7.1.5 Emaratech and its subsidiaries records shall be protected in accordance with
their corresponding information security classification, based on the
information classification scheme defined in Information Asset Management
Procedure (Document Number: ISD-ISMS-SPRC-09).
7.1.6 Records shall be categorized into record types (e.g. accounting records,
business transaction records, personnel records, legal records), each with
details of retention periods and type of allowable storage media which can be
physical or electronic.
Document Name Data Protection Policy
Applicable System Information Security Management System
Doc. No.: ISD-ISMS-SPOL-14 Version: 1.0 Issue Date: 14/10/2024 Page 10 of 14
Classification: Confidential
7.1.7 Data storage systems shall be chosen such that required records can be
retrieved in an acceptable time frame and format, depending on the
requirements to be fulfilled.
7.1.8 Cryptographic keys and programs associated with encrypted archives or
digital signatures, shall be retained to enable decryption of the records for the
length of time the records are retained in accordance with Cryptography and
Key Management Policy (Document Number: ISD-ISMS-SPOL-13).
7.1.9 IT/IMD shall implement File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) solutions on all critical
systems to detect unauthorized changes to sensitive records.
7.2. Data Privacy and Protection of Personal Information
7.2.1 Emaratech and its subsidiaries shall implement adequate protection controls
to ensure that individuals' Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is safeguarded
against misuse.
7.2.2 PII shall not be disclosed to anyone without written consent from the individual,
except when required by a court of law or to comply with applicable laws and
regulations.
7.2.3 PII shall only be collected, used, and shared for business purposes in
accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
7.2.4 Communications that shall include personal or private information, such as
emails and phone calls, made through system and networks, shall be recorded,

and monitored only in accordance with defined instructions, and approvals,
and after informing the concerned individuals.
7.3. Data Masking
7.3.1 IT/IMD shall identify and protect sensitive data (e.g. PII) using techniques such
as data masking, pseudonymization or anonymization. Additional techniques
for data masking include:
a) encryption (requiring authorized users to have a key);
b) nulling or deleting characters (preventing unauthorized users from seeing
full messages);
c) varying numbers and dates;
d) substitution (changing one value for another to hide sensitive data);
e) replacing values with their hash.
7.3.2 IT/IMD shall ensure the following when implementing data masking techniques:
a) not granting all users access to all data, therefore designing queries and
masks to show only the minimum required data to the user;
b) there are cases where some data should not be visible to the user for some
records out of a set of data; in this case, designing and implementing a
mechanism for obfuscation of data;
c) any legal or regulatory requirements (e.g. requiring the masking of payment
cards' information during processing or storage).
Document Name Data Protection Policy
Applicable System Information Security Management System
Doc. No.: ISD-ISMS-SPOL-14 Version: 1.0 Issue Date: 14/10/2024 Page 12 of 14
Classification: Confidential
7.3.3 IT/IMD shall ensure the following using data masking, pseudonymization or
anonymization:
a) level of strength of data masking, pseudonymization or anonymization
according to the usage of the processed data;
b) access controls to the processed data;
c) agreements or restrictions on usage of the processed data;
d) prohibiting collating the processed data with other information to identify
the PII principal;
e) keeping track of providing and receiving the processed data.
7.4. Data Leakage Prevention
7.4.1 IT/IMD shall ensure the following to reduce the risk of data leakage:
a) identifying and classifying information to protect against leakage (e.g.
personal information,
b) pricing models and product designs);
c) monitoring channels of data leakage (e.g. email, file transfers, mobile
devices and portable storage devices);
d) acting to prevent information from leaking (e.g. quarantine emails
containing sensitive information).
7.4.2 Data leakage prevention tools shall be used to:
Document Name Data Protection Policy
Applicable System Information Security Management System
Doc. No.: ISD-ISMS-SPOL-14 Version: 1.0 Issue Date: 14/10/2024 Page 13 of 14
Classification: Confidential
a) identify and monitor sensitive information at risk of unauthorized disclosure
(e.g. in unstructured data on a user’s system);
b) detect the disclosure of sensitive information (e.g. when information is
uploaded to untrusted third-party cloud services or sent via email);
c) block user actions or network transmissions that expose sensitive
information (e.g. preventing the copying of database entries into a
spreadsheet).
7.4.3 IT/IMD shall restrict users’ ability to copy and paste or upload data to services,
devices and storage media outside of Emaratech and its subsidiaries.
7.4.4 If required, the information owner shall export the data by obtaining approval
from line manager and ISM. CISO approval is mandated for information that is
classified as ‘Sensitive’ and ‘Secret’
7.4.5 Taking screenshots or photographs of the screen shall be addressed through
terms and conditions, training and auditing.
7.4.6 Where data is backed up, IT/IMD shall ensure sensitive information is protected
using measures such as encryption, access control and physical protection of
the storage media holding the backup.

8. Review
This policy shall be reviewed once every 12 months as per the Document Control and
Record Management Procedure (Document Number: ISD-ISMS-SPRC-08) or
whenever there is a major change in the operating environment.
9. Exceptions
Any exceptions to this policy shall be reviewed and approved by the ISSC.
10. Compliance
Any users found to have violated this policy and meeting any of the below criteria
may be subject to disciplinary action, in compliance with Human Resource Security
Policy (Document Number: ISD-ISMS-SPOL-17),
10.1. The user is aware of related security policies, and investigation proves it was an
intended action.
10.2. The violation has or could have a huge impact on Emaratech, and its
subsidiaries based on Security Risk Analysis.
10.3. The security violation is being repeated by the same user.
